summary.text: Suburban RV gas furnaces are thermostat-controlled, forced-air propane heaters: on a call for heat the blower starts and the main burner lights automatically about 30 seconds later. After repeated failed ignition the furnace locks out, the blower runs 5 minutes and stops, and the thermostat must be reset.

models.text: The Suburban Gas Furnace Operation Guide (220902) applies to all Suburban gas furnaces; the product identity label on the unit lists its specifications, test standard and safety notices.

The SF-VH Ducting Guide (ml-011221) covers the SF-35VH(F)Q and SF-42VH(F)Q, which have ten possible duct ports; minimum duct quantities come from each furnace's Installation, Operation and Maintenance manual.
SF-20FQ (2551A): 20,000 BTU/h input, 12 V, 5.1 A draw, two 4-inch ducts required, 55 in² return air. It has a front (inside) gas connection and a small exterior vent terminal.
When replacing a furnace, check its data plate for BTUH input and choose the same or a close size. Do not oversize: too much capacity causes rapid cycling and reduced comfort.
Suburban 120 V electric wall heaters: hard-wired models SEHNB and SEHNW, corded models SEHCB and SEHCW. Model, serial and stock numbers are on the rating/data plate label on the side.

display.text: After the thermostat calls for heat the furnace motor does not start instantly; allow about 30 seconds. You will hear the blower start, and about 30 seconds later the main burner ignites. Never light it by hand.
A lockout (failure to ignite after multiple attempts) shows as the blower continuing to run for 5 minutes and then shutting off. The guide describes no display or flash code for it.
Electric wall heater: the ON/OFF switch on the right side lights in the ON ('I') position and goes dark at OFF ('O'). The thermostat knob sets room temperature, not outlet air temperature.

reset.text: Lockout reset: the system must be reset by resetting the interior thermostat.
If the burner does not light or no heat comes from the vents, repeat the start steps: confirm the propane valve is fully open, set the thermostat, and wait for the blower and burner.
To turn the furnace off, set the thermostat to its lowest setting, move the lever to OFF, then turn the manual or tank valve OFF. The valve resists at full OFF; do not force it.
Wall heater high-limit trip: after removing the cause, such as blocked inlet or outlet openings, put the ON/OFF switch at OFF ('O') and let the heater cool before operating it again.

checks.text: The propane gas valve must be fully open; never run the furnace with any gas valve partly open. The manual valve is on the furnace (inside or outside, by gas hook-up) or at the RV propane tanks.
The furnace has a valve shut-off switch; with it in the OFF position no gas flows to the burner and the furnace will not operate.

Inspect the furnace venting: it must be free of obstructions and soot and routed to the exterior. Check that no RV door can block the vent when open; if it can, do not run the furnace with that door open.
Inspect the return air inlet openings and remove restrictions. Keep the furnace area clean; lint from carpet or bedding means more frequent cleaning. Keep combustibles and flammable vapors away.
Never operate the furnace with the vent covered. Where a slide-out or pop-up can cover it, set the thermostat to OFF and shut off all electrical and gas supply. Do not fit screens over the vent.
Turn the furnace and all ignition systems OFF during any refueling and while the vehicle is moving or being towed. If leaving it unattended, set the thermostat OFF and close the manual or tank valve.
Inspect the furnace vent for soot monthly during the heating season; Suburban also recommends an annual inspection by a qualified service technician.
checks.locator: 'Is there any preventative maintenance required on furnaces?'

checks.text: Ducts ending in dead air space (holding tank compartments, cargo or toy-box areas) and ducts 2 inches or smaller do not count toward the required duct area.

Clearances on the furnace label are minimums; meeting only them may not leave enough return air. Suburban's example: a 72 in² grate passes the SF-35's 55 in² minimum, but the cabinet path measured only 34 in².
Place the thermostat centrally, usually near the entry door, close to the furnace return grate, on an inside wall, about 4-1/2 feet above the floor; one mounted too high is satisfied prematurely.

If the electric wall heater does not heat, check the circuit breaker, the ON/OFF switch position and the thermostat knob setting. Check it annually for dust; clear the front and back openings with power off and the element cool.

parts.text: Suburban's FAQ lists common no-ignition causes as low propane, a faulty igniter or control board, a blocked air intake or exhaust, and thermostat or wiring issues.
parts.locator: 'Why is my Suburban furnace not igniting?'

parts.text: The furnace blower motor is permanently lubricated and requires no oiling.
Generic replacement parts are not approved: Suburban says they void the warranty and violate the intent of the UL, CUL, AGA or CGA certifications. Genuine parts come from Suburban service centers.
Warm-air ducts and connectors must meet NFPA 1192 and UL 181; Suburban suggests UL 181 adhesive tape to seal duct leaks, particularly at the duct port.
The electric wall heater has safety high-limit switches that shut it down if it overheats. There are no serviceable parts inside, and the user must not open it.

callTech.text: If you smell gas: evacuate everyone, shut off gas at the container, do not touch electrical switches, phones or radios, do not start the engine or generator, and contact the gas supplier or a qualified technician.
callTech.locator: p. 3 'What To Do If You Smell Gas'

callTech.text: If no gas supplier or technician can be reached, call the fire department. Do not turn on the gas supply until the leaks have been repaired. Never operate the furnace if you smell propane.
After three attempts with no ignition, turn the furnace off and contact your dealer or an RV service agency. Do not keep cycling the furnace through the thermostat.

Soot on the vent means incomplete combustion: shut the furnace down immediately and contact your dealer or a qualified service person. Do the same if the furnace cycles erratically or delays on ignition.
If the furnace overheats or the gas supply fails to shut off, shut off the manual gas valve (if equipped) before shutting off the electrical supply.
All repairs and maintenance should be done by a dealer or qualified service technician; service must be by a qualified installer, service agency or gas supplier.
Low gas pressure (bad regulator or low tank) and low voltage can only be tested by a qualified service technician.
callTech.locator: 'What causes the majority of furnace problems?'

callTech.text: The electric wall heater may not be serviced or modified by the end user. If the problem is not solved, notify the installer or contact Suburban Customer Service with the serial number.
